subject: af-post
title: AF.POST.------TR.
description: Diagram in AF(D)-9 (Affinity Dynamics, Level One), first of two on book p81, paired with v2-p81-2. Accompanies Braxton's claim that 'it is possible to view the dynamic spectrum of people in a single culture as representing and manifesting the realness of affinity dynamics through the same context as we now ascribe to race.' (C)AF-POST (the concept of affinity postulation) is crossed with TR (transformation): the question is what affinity-postulation produces when crossed with transformation — the postulation being the new affinity-spectrum reading that replaces race-as-given. TR sits at the upper-left of the partner cluster, with INFO-DY (information dynamics) and PART (participation) on the upper-right output. RE-ST (restructuralism) sits between TR and AF-DY. AF-DY (affinity dynamics) functions as the central hub between subject and partner. SOC-RT (social reality) anchors the right margin. BIA (bias) feeds into AF-DY from the lower-left. DYM-SPT (dynamics-spectacle) and A-PR (all-purpose) form the lower-left chain. INFO-DY appears a second time on the lower middle (Braxton's diagrams sometimes name a node twice when it functions at two levels). AF-N (affinity-negation) and ALT-F (alternative functionalism) cluster on the lower-right output. Structural argument: affinity-postulation crossed with transformation is mediated through affinity-dynamics as the central hub — exactly the chapter's organizing concept. The doubled INFO-DY exposes Braxton's diagnostic that information-dynamics functions at two registers in any real transformation: as upper output (what people will perceive after) and as lower upstream (what feeds the new postulation). The diagram is the case that race-thinking blocks transformation precisely by preventing the affinity-dynamics hub from operating across the full spectrum.
